maxFailedAttempts.description: Failed password logins that lock a user name from one address, and the same number of failures that lock an address. Applies by default, independently of the brute force protection of Basic and token authentication
maxFailedAttempts.title: Maximum Failed Attempts

lockoutMinutes.description: How long a locked user name or address stays locked after the first lockout. Every further lockout without a quiet period doubles it, up to 24 hours
lockoutMinutes.title: Lockout Minutes

accountThrottle.description: Delay of password and token guesses for one user name from addresses the name has not signed in from. Only applies while the switch INGOT_LOGIN_ACCOUNT_THROTTLE is on; the thresholds here have no effect without it
accountThrottle.title: Account Throttle

threshold.description: Failed credentials for one user name, from any address, after which the next guess from a new address is delayed. The first delay is one second
threshold.title: Threshold

quietMinutes.description: Minutes without a failure after which the count of failures of a user name starts again at zero
quietMinutes.title: Quiet Minutes

maxDelaySeconds.description: Longest delay of one request. The delay doubles with every failure beyond the threshold and ends by itself; a success clears it
maxDelaySeconds.title: Maximum Delay Seconds

knownAddressDays.description: Days after its last sign-in during which an address counts as known for a user name. A known address is not delayed by the account key
knownAddressDays.title: Known Address Days

passwordPolicy.description: Rules for a password that a user or an administrator sets. None of them applies at sign-in
passwordPolicy.title: Password Policy

minLength.description: Fewest characters of a new password, counted as before in UTF-16 code units. Between 8 and 256. A higher value applies to the next password that is set; stored passwords are not checked again
minLength.title: Minimum Length

breachCheck.description: Check of a new password against lists of breached passwords. Off by default
breachCheck.title: Breached Password Check

mode.description: OFF makes no check. RANGE sends the first five characters of the SHA-1 of a new password to the range service and compares the rest here. OFFLINE compares with the file below. RANGE is an outside call
mode.title: Mode

file.description: OFFLINE only: a file with one SHA-1 hash in hexadecimal per line. It is read once at start, and the start fails when it cannot be read
file.title: File

rangeUrl.description: RANGE only: base address of the range service, ending in a slash. The five characters are appended to it. Must be an https address
rangeUrl.title: Range URL

failClosed.description: RANGE only: when the service does not answer, refuse the change with 503 and Retry-After. When off, the change is allowed and an audit event records the outage
failClosed.title: Fail Closed

idleTimeoutMinutes.description: Minutes a browser session may stay idle before its refresh token expires. 0 keeps the refresh lifetime as the only idle limit. Otherwise at least 5, and at most the refresh lifetime in minutes
idleTimeoutMinutes.title: Idle Timeout Minutes

mfa.description: Browser sessions that must hold a second factor. A covered user without a factor keeps the grace period, then gets a restricted session until a factor is enrolled. The covered user is recorded at the first sign-in after the policy covers them, so the grace is per user
mfa.title: Second Factor Policy

requiredForAdmins.description: Instance administrators, directly or through a team, must hold a second factor. Access tokens are not covered
requiredForAdmins.title: Required For Administrators

requiredForTeams.description: Members of these teams must hold a second factor. Names are team names, and direct membership counts
requiredForTeams.title: Required For Teams

graceDays.description: Days after a policy first covers a user during which that user may sign in without a second factor. Between 0 and 365
graceDays.title: Grace Days

stepUpMinutes.description: Minutes a second factor stays recent for sensitive actions. Between 1 and 60. The default is 5
stepUpMinutes.title: Step-Up Minutes

passkeyFirstFactor.description: Lets a passkey sign a user in without a password. Off by default; the passkey routes answer 404 while it is off
passkeyFirstFactor.title: Passkey First Factor
